rationale: Since RANK(net cash) ≈ 1 − RANK(net debt), this expression is mechanically the profitability z-score *minus* the already-archived NetDebtWeightedOperatingProfit, so it is a sign-flipped decomposition of a tested signal whose result is largely predictable as an RMW tilt plus the negated prior alpha rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The runway framing is coherent and the coverage fix over the archived coverage ratio is a real improvement, but adding a stock (che) to a flow (oibdp) means cash-rich firms will dominate the numerator, so the signal risks collapsing into the well-known cash-holdings/liquidity ratio and should be diagnosed against a cash/lct-only benchmark.

This is an unweighted difference of two separately published anomalies — gross profitability/assets (RMW) and net debt issuance (Spiess–Affleck-Graves, Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan external financing) — in incommensurate raw units, so any result is a rediscovery of known effects rather than evidence of a genuine profitability–financing interaction.

The mean-over-volatility distance-to-default structure is economically motivated and the rank aggregation sensibly handles the fat tails of oiadp/lt, though the two legs are individually close to known profitability and earnings-volatility anomalies and the 5-year VOL window will cost coverage, so incremental value over each leg alone must be demonstrated.

The MIN combiner is a genuinely different functional form that tests complementarity rather than substitutability and is a legitimate contrast to the multiplicative gate, but it shares its entire ingredient set with archived signals and, because MIN is flat whenever one leg is high, most cross-sectional variation will come from whichever leg is weaker — a dependency worth diagnosing.
